datasets.title: Satellite detected water extent over Banke District, Lumbini Province, Nepal as of 25 & 30 October 2022
datasets.description: UNOSAT code FL20221117NPL This map illustrates satellite-detected surface waters in Banke District, Lumbini Province, Nepal as observed from Sentinel-2 images acquired on 25 & 30 October 2022 (Cumulative). Within the analyzed area of about 4,000 km², a combined 33 km² of lands appear to be flooded on the 25th and the 30th of October 2022. Water extent appears to have decreased of about 26 km² since the 15th October 2022. Based on Worldpop population data and the detected surface waters, about 1,400 people are potentially exposed or living close to flooded areas, of which 1,400 are located in Duduwa and Narainapur Palikas. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/water-extent-over-banke-district-lumbini-province-nepal-as-of-25-30-october-2022]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts processed Sentinel-2 satellite imagery from 25 and 30 October 2022 to detect surface water extent through multi-temporal image comparison, identifying 33 km² of flooded land in Banke District. Population exposure was estimated by overlaying detected water extent with WorldPop gridded population data, yielding approximately 1,400 potentially affected people.
